Dylan: Heads-up — hitting steadily growing GPU memory + PT entries during our long-context synthetic chat on MI250X. Eviction runs but PT entry count keeps climbing over the session. Repro below, minimal run. @Arjun :eyes:

Dylan: Repro command I used:
```bash
# run from infra/tests/kv_pager
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./kv_pager_load --model=llama-2-13b --seq-len=65536 --steps=450 --batch-size=4 --page-size=64k --force-pmigrate
```
This spikes after ~200 steps and never comes back down even when we trigger full eviction. Logs attached in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kv-mi250x-trace

Arjun: Can you paste the eviction logs (`kvcache evict` trace) and the PT summary (`pt stats`) output? Also which driver/ROCm version?

Dylan: driver: ROCm 5.7, kernel 6.1. Evict trace snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T03:12:45Z] evict: pages_requested=8192 pages_evicted=4096 stalled=0
[2026-03-16T03:12:47Z] migrate: moved=2048 dst_gpu=1 src_gpu=0 ref_inc=2048
[2026-03-16T03:12:47Z] pt: entries=1,048,576 free_slots=32,768 frag=12%
[2026-03-16T03:12:50Z] evict: pages_requested=8192 pages_evicted=2048 stalled=3
[2026-03-16T03:12:52Z] pt: entries=1,097,152 free_slots=16,384 frag=18%
```
So PT entries up ~48k in seconds.

Kevin: Sounds like a refcount leak on migration or an ownership flip that doesn't decrement the old owner's ref. We saw similar on NVLink path but never this fast. Any difference in batching?

Dylan: We only see it when `--batch-size >= 4` and when the batching heuristic switches to aggressive coalescing (the runtime chooses `batch_coalesce=true` path). If I cap batch to 2, PT growth is steady and stable. So interplay between batching heuristic and migration looks suspicious.

Sophia: I pulled a flamegraph from the run (pprof -> flame.svg). Top hotspots are `kvcache::insert_page`, `kvcache::migrate_async`, and a long tail in `pt_walk()` where it spins on `atomic_cmpxchg` on the entry metadata. Might be ABA-ish on the PT owner tag.

AJ: Hypothesis: when coalesced batches cause concurrent migrations of adjacent pages, we race on writing PT meta; one writer sets owner, the other backs off but doesn't clear an intermediate transient ref. On NV we had fence ordering fixes; on ROCm the memory ordering may be weaker for our atomic ops.

Arjun: Can you run with KV_PAGER_DEBUG=1 and REDWOOD_KV_PAGER_SERIALIZE=0/1 toggled and attach the `pt ops` trace? Also try the micro repro I checked in: `tests/kv_pager/migrate_race_repro.cc` (quick build target `kv_migrate_repro`).

Dylan: Ran KV_PAGER_DEBUG=1. Trace excerpt:
```
[dbg] allocate page id=0x7fffa1 ref=1 owner=0
[dbg] migrate start id=0x7fffa1 src=0 dst=1 opid=42
[dbg] migrate commit id=0x7fffa1 owner=1 ref++ => 2
[dbg] migrate start id=0x7fffa2 src=0 dst=1 opid=43
[dbg] migrate abort id=0x7fffa1 owner=1 ref-- => 1   # expected
[dbg] migrate commit id=0x7fffa2 owner=1 ref++ => 2
[warn] pt entry leak detected id=0x7fffa1 ref=1 persisted after free
```
We see an aborted migrate that should decrement but there's a window where other ops re-increment; the aborted path doesn't always decrement due to an early return in the async callback.

Kevin: That callback path rings true. On H100 we had a `kvcache::migrate_cleanup()` in the callback which always decremented refs; ROCm callback code path may be skipping when `status == MIGRATE_REDIRECT`.

Sophia: Quick perf numbers: when the leak reproduces, token throughput drops ~22% and latency p50 increases 18% — likely due to extra pagewalks and PT scanning. I can add a regression test to track PT growth over long context runs.

Arjun: For immediate triage: 1) Try `export REDWOOD_KVCACHE_SERIALIZE=1` (this forces single-threaded page move commits). 2) Run the `kv_migrate_repro` with `--stress-migrate` for 10k ops. 3) Patch proposal: ensure `migrate_abort` always calls `dec_ref()` in the deferred path before return.

Dylan: I tried `REDWOOD_KVCACHE_SERIALIZE=1` — PT stops growing and system stabilizes. Workaround confirmed. Added to runbook.

AJ: I'll open PR `fix/migrate-decref-rocm` with the dec-ref in the abort path and add a stress test. I think we should also add an atomic owner-tag version bump to avoid ABA.

Sophia: I'll add a nightly regression that runs the long-context scenario with batch sizes 1..8 across H100/MI250X and fail the job if PT entries increase >1% over 1h.

Dylan: Thanks everyone. Next steps: AJ PR -> land after CI, Sophia adds regression, Arjun please run NV compare to make sure we didn't mask anything. @oncall please monitor `kvcache.pt.entries` metric for the next 2 deployments. :party:
